story: Radha was a gopi, a cowherd girl of Vrindavan, and Krishna's beloved in his youth. Their love, and the raas leela danced under the full moon, is the heart of countless songs and poems. When Krishna left for Mathura, he never came back to her.
belief: In many Vaishnava traditions, Radha is the greatest devotee and the very power of Krishna. Devotees greet each other with 'Radhe Radhe', and loving God the way Radha loved Krishna is seen as the highest devotion.
turns: She is known less for mistakes than for pain: she loved without holding back and was left behind. Poets also describe her maan, a proud, jealous sulk toward Krishna, as part of the drama of divine love.
facts: Radha is not named in the Mahabharata or the Bhagavata Purana; she becomes central in later works like Jayadeva's Gita Govinda (12th century).
Barsana, her village, is famous for Lathmar Holi.
lessons: Love that asks for nothing is the purest.
Missing someone can be a form of devotion.
Joy is worth sharing even when it can't last.
more: In many temples she is worshipped together with Krishna as Radha-Krishna.
In Vrindavan, devotees speak her name before his: 'Radhe Krishna'.
